indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: A, then H, hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone takes care phoning a hotel in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind ringing' reads as not minding phoning; 'ringing' means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf, one of the Gulf states.

clue.text: With energy, married couple perhaps do this?

definitions.text: With energy, married couple perhaps do this?

blocks.note: joins the energy to the rest
part of the whole-clue reading only

explanation.surface: A newly married pair throw their arms round each other enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a keen married couple might well hug, and brace is a pair, as of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace is to hold someone closely in your arms, what a loving pair do.

clue.text: Return from India, packing cases for 19 and Lapland

indicators.note: packing puts things inside a case, so one letter goes within another pair
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: 19 down is the Cameroonian capital, whose ends are these

explanation.surface: Travellers come back from India, having packed bags for Cameroon and Lapland.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'cases' act on two words: the capital from 19 and Lapland. The capital's ends pack the India letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A return on an investment is the profit it makes, which is also called its yield.

clue.text: Hard to climb flipping frame of Eiffel Tower!

indicators.note: a frame is the outer border, so only the first and last letters are kept
flipping turns something over, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: a steep slope is hard to climb

explanation.surface: An exasperated climber finds the Eiffel Tower's framework too hard to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, as in 'flipping heck'; it is the reversal signal. 'Tower' is split off from Eiffel to be the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a tall tower on a church, often topped by a spire.

clue.text: Gift yours truly wrapped in blue taken into part of hospital

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it
whatever is taken into a place ends up inside it

blocks.note: the ear, nose and throat department
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A present for me, gift-wrapped in blue, is carried into a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' reads as wrapping-paper colour; it means sad. Two containers nest, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a gift of money or property to an institution, such as a donation funding a college.
